asker_query: Sister, the family does not want my mother to be told it is cancer — they think she will lose hope. But now she is directly asking me, 'is it cancer, tell me truth'. What do I do? Can we keep hiding? Or do we tell her?
answer:
The patient has a right to know her diagnosis, but disclosure requires sensitivity. First, assess her understanding of "cancer" (e.g., fear of agonizing death) and explain that treatments can manage symptoms and improve quality of life, even if curative options are limited {}. Family collusion to withhold information often stems from fear of causing harm but risks patient anxiety or distrust {}. Share information in digestible chunks, addressing her emotions and offering hope (e.g., ongoing care, symptom relief) {}. Facilitate a joint discussion with the family and healthcare providers to align on communication strategies
